xin.metaTitle: Lodging a claim in a Slovak bankruptcy — foreign creditors
xin.metaDescription: Slovak customer in bankruptcy or restructuring: a 45- or 30-day deadline, lodging the claim with the trustee, denial of the claim. Law firm in Zvolen.
xin.heroTitle: Your Slovak customer is in bankruptcy or restructuring
xin.heroLead: From publication in the Slovak Insolvency Register, a period for lodging your claim runs: 45 days in bankruptcy, 30 days in restructuring. We check the status of the proceedings, prepare and lodge the claim, and represent you in dealings with the trustee, before the court and at the creditors’ meeting.
heroPara: We act for foreign companies with unpaid invoices for goods, carriage or works against a Slovak customer in respect of which a Slovak court has declared bankruptcy, authorised restructuring or — in the case of a natural person — decided on debt relief (oddlženie). A lawyer of the firm is entered in the list of trustees kept by the Ministry of Justice of the Slovak Republic.
We work in English and Slovak and can run the whole matter remotely.
xin.whoLead: We represent foreign creditors in proceedings conducted by a Slovak court under Act No. 7/2005 Coll. on bankruptcy and restructuring. We advise exclusively on Slovak law; questions governed by the law of another country — for example the validity of the contract or of a retention of title under foreign law — we handle in cooperation with the client’s lawyer in the client’s own country.

who.title: Suppliers with unpaid invoices
who.desc: Goods, carriage, construction subcontracts or services supplied to a Slovak company that is in bankruptcy or restructuring. A claim that arose before the declaration of bankruptcy is asserted by lodging it with the trustee (prihláška pohľadávky) — litigation over it is stayed and enforcement is discontinued.

who.title: Suppliers with retention of title
who.desc: Goods which, under the contract, are to remain your property until paid for in full and which are in the debtor’s possession. A choice has to be made between having the item excluded from the inventory of assets and lodging a claim, which gives you a position similar to that of a secured creditor.

who.title: Creditors holding security
who.desc: A pledge over the debtor’s assets, a third-party guarantee or other security. A security right over the debtor’s assets has to be asserted directly in the lodgement of the claim and within the basic period, otherwise it is disregarded in the bankruptcy. Claims against guarantors remain preserved even after confirmation of the restructuring plan (Section 155(4)) and after the debtor’s debt relief (Section 166e(3)).

who.title: Creditors of a sole trader in debt relief
who.desc: The debtor is a natural person carrying on business (in Slovakia typically a sole trader — živnostník) who is seeking debt relief. Debt relief also covers claims that the creditor has not lodged: a creditor that does not lodge receives nothing from the bankruptcy, and the unsatisfied part of the claim becomes unenforceable against the debtor.

xin.keyTitle: The deadlines and rules that matter
xin.keyLead: Slovak law has three collective proceedings that a foreign creditor encounters: bankruptcy (konkurz — the debtor’s assets are realised and creditors are satisfied proportionately), restructuring (reštrukturalizácia — the business continues and creditors are satisfied under a plan on which they vote and which the court confirms) and debt relief of a natural person (oddlženie). All three are governed by Act No. 7/2005 Coll. on bankruptcy and restructuring, and all three are insolvency proceedings under Annex A to Regulation (EU) 2015/848 of the European Parliament and of the Council on insolvency proceedings. Under Article 7 of the Regulation, the proceedings and their effects are governed by the law of the State in which they were opened — the rules on lodging, verification and ranking of claims are therefore Slovak even where the contract with the customer itself is governed by another law. In each of these proceedings the court appoints a trustee (správca): a person entered in the list of trustees kept by the Ministry of Justice, who administers the debtor’s assets in bankruptcy, supervises the debtor’s business in restructuring (Section 129(1)) and examines the lodged claims. Under Section 199(1) of the Act, decisions and documents of the court and of the trustee are served by publication in the Insolvency Register, which is publicly accessible on the Ministry’s website. The periods for lodging claims run from that publication, not from the moment the creditor learned of the proceedings: the basic period is 45 days from the declaration of bankruptcy and 30 days from the authorisation of restructuring.

key.title: Bankruptcy: 45 days from publication in the Insolvency Register
key.desc: Under Section 28(2) of Act No. 7/2005 Coll., a claim is lodged within the basic period for lodging claims, that is, within 45 days of the declaration of bankruptcy. Under Section 23(1), bankruptcy is declared by publication of the court’s order (uznesenie) declaring bankruptcy in the Insolvency Register; under Section 199(7), a document is deemed published on the day following its publication in the Register. The day that determines the start of the period is not counted in it, and if the last day falls on a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday, the last day of the period is the next working day (Section 203a(1) and (2)). For a foreign creditor the key rule is Section 203a(3): the period is observed if the submission is delivered to its addressee no later than the last day of the period — dispatching it on that day is not enough. Under Section 197(3), the Act does not allow a missed deadline to be excused. A lodgement delivered after the period is not lost: under Section 28(3) it is taken into account, but the creditor cannot exercise the voting right or the other rights attached to the lodged claim and can be satisfied only from proceeds included in a distribution from the general estate where the intention to draw it up was announced in the Insolvency Register only after the lodgement was delivered. The creditor therefore does not share in distributions announced earlier.
key.note: Under Section 30(2) of the Act, a submission by which a claim has been asserted cannot be corrected or supplemented, and under Section 29(1) a lodgement that was not made in the prescribed manner or does not contain the basic particulars is disregarded. A new lodgement made after the basic period has expired is already a late lodgement, with the consequences under Section 28(3). We therefore do not recommend preparing the lodgement in the last days of the period.

key.title: With whom, in what form and in what language
key.desc: The claim is lodged not with the court but with the trustee. As a general rule it is lodged exclusively electronically, by an authorised form sent to the trustee’s electronic mailbox. For a foreign creditor within the meaning of Article 2(12) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848 — a creditor which has its habitual residence, domicile or registered office in another Member State — Section 28(2) of the Act lays down a special regime: the claim is lodged with the trustee, and the Civil Contentious Procedure Code applies mutatis mutandis to service; a creditor with its registered office outside the Member States lodges its claim in the same way. The Regulation adds three safeguards. Under Article 53, a foreign creditor may lodge a claim by any means of communication accepted by the law of the State of the opening of proceedings, and representation by a lawyer is not mandatory for the sole purpose of lodging the claim. Under Article 55(1), it may use the standard claims form headed “Lodgement of claims”, set out in Annex II to Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1105; if it does not use it, the claim must, under Article 55(4), contain the information listed in Article 55(2). And under Article 55(5), a claim may be lodged in any official language of the institutions of the Union, although the court or the trustee may require a translation into Slovak. Under Section 29(1) of the Act, the basic particulars of a lodgement are identification of the creditor and of the bankrupt (úpadca), the legal basis of the claim, the ranking for satisfaction from the general estate, and the total amount of the claim, which under Section 29(4) is broken down into principal and ancillary claims (príslušenstvo), with the ancillary claims broken down further by the legal basis on which they arose. The claim is asserted in euros; if it is asserted in another currency, the trustee determines the amount by conversion at the reference exchange rate determined and published by the European Central Bank or the National Bank of Slovakia on the day bankruptcy was declared (Section 29(5)). Documents proving the facts stated are attached to the lodgement, and a creditor that is an accounting entity declares in it whether and to what extent it carries the claim in its accounts (Section 29(6)).
key.note: A creditor that has no habitual residence, domicile or registered office in the territory of the Slovak Republic is obliged under Section 29(8) of the Act to appoint a representative for service with a domicile, habitual residence or registered office in Slovakia and to notify the trustee of this — otherwise documents are served on it by publication in the Insolvency Register. Where the claim is lodged by a representative and the power of attorney is not attached to it, the lodgement is disregarded under Section 28(2). The right under Article 53 of the Regulation to lodge without a lawyer concerns only the lodging of the claim itself.

key.title: What bankruptcy changes about recovery: litigation, enforcement, set-off, security
key.desc: Under Section 47(1) of the Act, the declaration of bankruptcy stays all court and other proceedings that concern assets subject to the bankruptcy belonging to the bankrupt — and so also an action in which a foreign supplier is suing for payment of its invoices. Under Section 48, enforcement proceedings cannot be commenced against assets subject to the bankruptcy during the bankruptcy, and enforcement proceedings already commenced are discontinued upon the declaration of bankruptcy; if the enforcement officer has already realised assets but has not yet paid the proceeds out to the creditor, the proceeds become part of the bankruptcy estate. From then on the claim is asserted by lodging it (Section 28(1)), and under Section 28(6) lodging has the same effects on the running of the limitation period and on the extinction of the right as asserting the right in court. Bankruptcy does not rule out set-off altogether, but restricts it: under Section 54(1), a claim that arose against the bankrupt before the declaration of bankruptcy cannot be set off against a claim of the bankrupt that arose only after it, and under Section 54(2) a claim that has not been lodged cannot be set off against any claim of the bankrupt. Anyone wishing to set off must therefore lodge first. A secured creditor must also assert the security right in the lodgement properly and in time — within the basic 45-day period — otherwise it is disregarded in the bankruptcy (Section 28(4)); a separate lodgement is made for each secured claim, stating the secured amount and the type, ranking, subject matter and legal basis of the security right (Section 29(2)). A creditor whose claim is against another person but is secured by assets of the bankrupt must lodge as well (Section 28(7) and (8)).
key.note: Under Section 28(5), a future or conditional claim can also be lodged — for example a claim arising from withdrawal from a contract under Section 45(2) of the Act; the lodgement must state the fact or condition on which the claim depends (Section 29(3)). A contractual penalty, and a claim of a creditor that is, or at any time since the claim arose was, related to the bankrupt — for example a shareholder with a qualifying holding of at least 5 % under Section 9 — are, under Section 95(3), satisfied only as subordinated claims, and security for them is disregarded in the bankruptcy. For assets that were situated in another Member State at the time of the opening of proceedings, creditors’ rights in rem and retention of title are protected by Articles 8 and 10 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848.

key.title: Denial of the claim and the action for determination of the denied claim (incidenčná žaloba)
key.desc: The trustee examines each lodged claim and compares it with the debtor’s accounts and records (Section 32(1)). A claim may be denied by the trustee or by another creditor that has lodged a claim — as to its legal basis, enforceability, amount, ranking, security or the ranking of the security right (Section 32(2)) — within 30 days of the expiry of the basic period for lodging claims or, in the case of a late lodgement, within 30 days of its entry in the list of claims (Section 32(3)); for the trustee the court may extend the period, even repeatedly, each time by no more than 30 days (Section 32(4)). A claim not denied within the period is deemed established (Section 32(16)). The creditor of a denied claim must seek its determination by an action in court against all those who denied it, within 30 days of publication of the denial in the list of claims, otherwise that right is extinguished (Section 32(8)) and the trustee records, to the extent of the denial, the end of the creditor’s status as a party to the proceedings (Section 27(2)(c)). The period is observed even where the action was filed in time with a court that lacks jurisdiction. The action may seek no more than was stated in the lodgement (Section 32(13)). The period runs from publication of the denial in the list of claims in the Insolvency Register, not from delivery of a letter to the creditor — the Register therefore has to be monitored once the period for lodging claims has expired.
key.note: Where the claim was denied only by another creditor, a condition for filing the action is proper and timely payment of an advance on the costs of the proceedings (Section 32(10)): two per cent of the amount of the disputed claim or, where only the amount is denied, two per cent of the denied amount, not less than 350 euros and not more than 10 000 euros (Section 32(19)). An advance in the same amount is also paid by a creditor that denies another creditor’s claim (Section 32(6)(b)). A person who denied a claim that the court upheld even in part is liable to its creditor for the damage caused by the denial, unless that person proves that it acted with professional care (Section 32(5)). For a claim awarded by an enforceable decision or secured by a registered pledge, the court may be asked, through the trustee, to grant voting rights even while the dispute is pending (Section 32a).

key.title: Restructuring: 30 days and no late lodgement
key.desc: In restructuring the claim must be lodged within 30 days of the authorisation of the restructuring, otherwise it is disregarded (Section 121); restructuring is authorised by publication of the court’s order in the Insolvency Register (Section 118(1)). Unlike in bankruptcy, there is no such thing as late lodging here. The consequence is strict: under Section 120(1) and Section 155(2), upon publication of the order confirming the plan, the right of a creditor that did not lodge its claim properly and in time to recover it from the debtor is extinguished, as are security rights over the debtor’s assets that were not lodged properly and in time. Only so-called priority claims (prednostné pohľadávky) are not asserted by lodging, in particular those that arose only during the restructuring proceedings (Section 120(2)). The manner of lodging is the same as in bankruptcy (Section 121), and the particulars of the lodgement are governed mutatis mutandis by Section 29(1) to (6) and (8) — and so also by the rules on conversion of foreign currency and on the representative for service (Section 122(1)); a security right not asserted in the lodgement means that the claim is treated as unsecured in the restructuring. The commencement of restructuring proceedings — that is, even before the restructuring is authorised — already has effects which a supplier feels immediately (Section 114(1)): for a claim that is asserted by lodging, enforcement cannot be commenced and enforcement already commenced is stayed, such a claim cannot be set off against the debtor, and the other contracting party cannot terminate the contract by notice or withdraw from it on account of the debtor’s delay with a performance to which that party became entitled before the commencement of the proceedings; contractual provisions that would allow the contract to be terminated on the ground of restructuring proceedings or bankruptcy proceedings are also ineffective. A party that is to perform first under the contract may refuse performance until the counter-performance is provided or secured (Section 114(3)). The authorisation of the restructuring stays court and arbitration proceedings concerning the claims being lodged (Section 118(4)).
key.note: In restructuring a claim may be denied only by the trustee, within 30 days of the expiry of the period for lodging claims (Section 124(2)). The creditor of a denied claim must, within 30 days of the expiry of the period for denying claims, file an action against the debtor (Section 124(4)), otherwise the claim is disregarded to the extent denied and, after confirmation of the plan, cannot be recovered from the debtor to that extent (Section 124(5)). Creditors vote on the plan in groups at the plan approval meeting; the required majorities are laid down in Section 148. The court rejects the plan, among other cases, where any unsecured claim — other than those that would be satisfied as subordinated claims in bankruptcy — is to be satisfied as to less than 50 % or over a period longer than five years, unless the creditor concerned consents in writing (Section 154(1)(g) and (h)). Rights against the debtor’s co-debtors and guarantors remain unaffected by the plan (Section 155(4)).

key.title: The debtor is a sole trader or a small company: debt relief and small bankruptcy
key.desc: Where the debtor is a natural person — including an entrepreneur, in Slovakia typically a sole trader (živnostník) — that person may, under Section 166(1) of the Act, seek debt relief by bankruptcy or by a repayment schedule, regardless of whether the obligations stem from business. Claims that arose before the calendar month in which bankruptcy was declared or protection from creditors was granted can be satisfied only in the bankruptcy or under the repayment schedule, and in the bankruptcy they are asserted by lodging (Section 166a). The court decides on debt relief already in the order declaring bankruptcy or determining the repayment schedule (Section 166e(1)), and under Section 166e(2) these claims become unenforceable against the debtor regardless of whether or not they were lodged. The exception for a creditor whom the trustee did not notify in writing of the declaration of bankruptcy applies, under Section 166c(1)(a), only to creditors who are natural persons; a foreign company cannot rely on it. The claim is lodged within the basic period of 45 days from the declaration of bankruptcy; later it can still be lodged until the trustee publishes a notice of the intention to draw up a distribution schedule, but the creditor cannot exercise the voting right (Section 167l(1) and (3)). The court discontinues court proceedings concerning such claims (Section 167e(1)), and enforcement against assets subject to the bankruptcy can be neither commenced nor continued (Section 167f(1)).
key.note: In debt relief, what is unenforceable against the debtor under Section 166b(1) includes, among other things, ancillary claims exceeding 5 % of the principal for each calendar year of the claim’s existence, and contractual penalties. A secured claim remains unaffected by debt relief to the extent that it is covered by the value of the subject matter of the security right (Section 166c(1)(c)), and the claim remains enforceable against a guarantor (Section 166e(3)). A creditor affected by the debt relief may, within six years of the declaration of bankruptcy or the determination of the repayment schedule, seek cancellation of the debt relief if it proves that the debtor did not have an honest intent (Section 166f(1)). Small bankruptcy (malý konkurz) is a simplified bankruptcy of a legal person neither the liabilities nor the assets of which exceeded 1 000 000 euros according to its last five financial statements (Section 106c(1)(f) and (g)); the court states in the operative part of the order that it is a small bankruptcy (Section 106c(4)). Section 167l applies mutatis mutandis to the lodging and denial of claims in it (Section 106h) — a claim can therefore be denied only by another creditor that has lodged a claim (Section 167l(5)). A creditor that has lodged a claim may, within six months of the declaration of small bankruptcy, by paying an advance, have the court declare bankruptcy under the general provisions (Section 106j(1)).

steps.title: Checking the status of the proceedings
steps.desc: In the Slovak Insolvency Register we check which proceedings are under way — bankruptcy, small bankruptcy, restructuring or debt relief — when the order was published, who the trustee is and when the period for lodging claims expires. Under Articles 24, 25 and 27 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848, the mandatory information on the proceedings, including the time limit for lodging claims, is also to be available free of charge via the European e-Justice Portal, with a search service in all the official languages of the institutions of the Union. We do not recommend waiting for the individual notice from the trustee under Article 54 of the Regulation: the periods under the Slovak Act run from publication in the Register. At the same time we establish what effect the proceedings have on your litigation or enforcement against the debtor.

steps.title: Calculating the claim and lodging it
steps.desc: We quantify the principal and the ancillary claims by legal basis, convert foreign currency into euros, determine the ranking and — if you hold security or a retention of title — agree with you how to assert it. We deliver the lodgement, with its annexes and the power of attorney, to the trustee so that it reaches the trustee before the period expires. As a firm established in Slovakia, we can also act as your representative for service under Section 29(8) of the Act.

steps.title: Examination of claims and defence against denial
steps.desc: During the period for denying claims we monitor the list of claims in the Insolvency Register and communicate with the trustee. If the claim is denied, we file an action for its determination within the 30-day period. Where there is reason to do so, we propose that you deny claims of other creditors that unjustifiably reduce your share; this entails paying an advance on the costs of the proceedings.

steps.title: Creditors’ meeting and creditors’ committee
steps.desc: The trustee convenes the first creditors’ meeting within 55 days of the declaration of bankruptcy so that it is held no earlier than 30 and no later than 45 days after the expiry of the period for denying claims (Section 34(1)). A creditor whose claim is established as to its legal basis and enforceability has the right to vote — one vote for each euro of the established amount (Section 35(4)). The meeting decides on replacing the trustee (Section 36) and elects a creditors’ committee of three or five members (Section 37(1)), which gives the trustee binding instructions on the administration and realisation of the assets of the general estate (Section 82). We represent you at the meeting; the Act also allows a meeting to be held by videoconference (Section 34(5)). In restructuring we represent the creditor at the creditors’ meeting (Section 126) and in the vote on the plan at the plan approval meeting (Sections 147 and 148).

steps.title: Distribution and payment
steps.desc: Before drawing up the distribution schedule the trustee publishes a notice of the intention to draw it up (Section 96(2)); on the basis of the approved distribution schedule the trustee pays out the undisputed part of the proceeds to the creditors (Section 96(5)). We check that your claim is included in the distribution schedule in the correct amount and ranking, and give the trustee the details needed for payment abroad. Under Section 96(7), the creditor itself bears the costs of satisfaction of its claim.

xin.docsLead: Send what you have available as scans or photographs; originals are not needed at this stage. The documents may be in your language — we will tell you which of them will need to be translated into Slovak.
docs: The contract, framework agreement or purchase orders, including the terms and conditions — in particular the provisions on the applicable law, payment terms, default interest and retention of title.
Unpaid invoices and proof of delivery: delivery notes, CMR consignment notes, handover protocols, statements of work performed.
A statement of payments and the outstanding balance of the claim from your accounts — the lodgement contains a declaration of whether and to what extent you carry the claim in your accounts.
Court decisions, payment orders and other enforcement titles against the debtor, and information on pending litigation and enforcement proceedings.

Security documents: the pledge agreement and confirmation of registration of the pledge, the guarantor’s declaration and, for retention of title, precise identification of the goods and of the place where they are located.
Acknowledgements of debt, instalment agreements, mutual set-offs and correspondence with the debtor about the claim.
Everything you have received from the trustee or the court — in particular the “Notice of insolvency proceedings” under Article 54 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848.
An extract from the commercial or equivalent register for your company, and details of the person who will sign the power of attorney.
xin.priceLead: The scope and the fee are agreed in advance and in writing. You know the price for checking the proceedings and for lodging the claim before we start work.

price.label: Checking the proceedings and assessing the matter
price.desc: We check the status of the proceedings in the Insolvency Register, calculate the deadline, go through the documents and set out the procedure we propose. We quote the fee before any work starts; if you decide not to go ahead, the matter ends there.

price.label: Lodging the claim
price.desc: Quantifying the claim, preparing the lodgement with its annexes and delivering it to the trustee, including asserting the security right. Agreed as a fixed sum for the step, not at an hourly rate.

price.label: Dispute over a denied claim and further representation
price.desc: Under Section 7(1) of Decree of the Ministry of Justice of the Slovak Republic No. 655/2004 Coll., a contingency fee may be agreed in the form of a percentage share in the value of the matter; under Section 7(2) its maximum amount may not exceed 20 % of that value. Under Section 8(1) of the Decree it becomes payable only where the client has been fully successful in the matter; where the client is partly successful the lawyer is entitled under Section 8(2) to the tariff fee determined according to the degree of success, and where the client has not been successful even in part the lawyer may under Section 8(3) claim only reimbursement of out-of-pocket expenses.

xin.priceNote: Out-of-pocket expenses arise alongside the lawyer’s fee, in particular translations into Slovak if the trustee or the court requires them (Article 55(5) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848). The claimant in proceedings for determination of a denied claim and the claimant in proceedings for exclusion of assets from the inventory are exempt from the court fee under Section 4(2)(t) and (q) of Act No. 71/1992 Coll. on court fees. Where the claim was denied only by another creditor, however, an advance on the costs of the proceedings has to be paid before the action is filed, in the amount of two per cent of the disputed amount, not less than 350 euros and not more than 10 000 euros (Section 32(10) and (19) of Act No. 7/2005 Coll.). In these proceedings a successful represented party is entitled to reimbursement of the tariff fee as for representation in enforcement (Section 32(11)). The outcome of proceedings depends on the circumstances of the individual case, in particular on the debtor’s assets, the amount of the other claims and the ranking of your claim.
xin.formTitle: Send us the details of the debtor and the claim
xin.formLead: Tell us who the debtor is, what claim you have against it and what you have learned about the proceedings — and, if you know it, the date of publication in the Insolvency Register. The deadlines are short and the Act does not allow a missed deadline to be excused, so we recommend writing without delay. We will get back to you and set out the next steps. Submitting this form does not create a lawyer-client relationship.

faq.q: We learned of the bankruptcy late. Have we missed the deadline?
faq.a: It depends on the type of proceedings. In the bankruptcy of a legal person a lodgement delivered after the 45-day period is taken into account, but under Section 28(3) of Act No. 7/2005 Coll. the creditor cannot exercise the voting right or the other rights attached to the claim and shares only in distributions from the general estate where the intention to draw them up was announced in the Insolvency Register after the lodgement was delivered; a security right asserted after the period is disregarded (Section 28(4)). In the bankruptcy of a natural person and in small bankruptcy, a claim can be lodged until the trustee publishes a notice of the intention to draw up a distribution schedule (Section 167l(1)). In restructuring a claim lodged after the 30 days is disregarded (Section 121), and after confirmation of the plan the claim cannot be recovered from the debtor (Section 155(2)). The Act does not allow a missed deadline to be excused (Section 197(3)). Regulation (EU) 2015/848 requires the court or the trustee to inform known foreign creditors immediately by an individual notice, which also states the time limits (Article 54), and provides in Article 55(6) that the period for a foreign creditor must not be less than 30 days following the publication of the opening of insolvency proceedings in the insolvency register; the period itself, however, it leaves to the law of the State of the opening of proceedings. What significance the fact that no notice arrived has in a particular matter has to be assessed individually — so get in touch as soon as you learn of the proceedings.

faq.q: Can we lodge the claim in English or in another EU language, for example Polish?
faq.a: Under Article 55(5) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848, claims may be lodged in any official language of the institutions of the Union; both English and Polish are among them under Article 1 of Regulation No 1 of 1958. The court or the trustee may, however, require the creditor to provide a translation into the official language of the State of the opening of proceedings, that is, into Slovak. The standard claims form “Lodgement of claims” is Annex II to Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1105, and using it is the creditor’s right, not an obligation (Article 55(1) and (4)). These rules apply to creditors from other Member States of the Union. We prepare the lodgement in Slovak, so that the trustee does not need to ask for a translation and so that it also contains the information required by the Slovak Act — the legal basis of the claim, the ranking, the breakdown into principal and ancillary claims, and the declaration on whether the claim is carried in the accounts (Section 29 of Act No. 7/2005 Coll.).

faq.q: Our claim is in zloty, Czech koruna or dollars. How is it lodged?
faq.a: Under Section 29(5) of Act No. 7/2005 Coll., a claim is asserted in euros. If the creditor asserts it in another currency, the trustee determines the amount by conversion at the reference exchange rate determined and published by the European Central Bank or the National Bank of Slovakia on the day bankruptcy was declared; for a currency for which no such rate is determined, the trustee determines the amount with professional care. What counts, therefore, is the rate on the day bankruptcy was declared, not the rate on the date of the invoice or on the date of payment. In restructuring this rule applies mutatis mutandis (Section 122(1)). In the distribution a creditor cannot be awarded more than it asserted in the lodgement (Section 96(1)), so we carry out and document the conversion when preparing the lodgement.

faq.q: The trustee has denied our claim. What now?
faq.a: Denial does not mean that the claim has ceased to exist, but it triggers a short deadline. Under Section 32(8) of Act No. 7/2005 Coll., the creditor must seek determination of the denied claim by an action in court against all those who denied it, within 30 days of publication of the denial in the list of claims, otherwise that right is extinguished; the period is observed even where the action is filed in time with a court that lacks jurisdiction. The action may seek no more than was stated in the lodgement (Section 32(13)). A claim denied only by the trustee may be acknowledged by the trustee in writing until the court has decided on its determination (Section 32(17)) — so, alongside preparing the action, it is worth supplying the trustee with the missing documents. Where the claim was denied only by another creditor, payment of an advance on the costs of the proceedings is a condition for the action (Section 32(10) and (19)). The claimant in these proceedings is exempt from the court fee (Section 4(2)(t) of Act No. 71/1992 Coll.). In restructuring the action is filed against the debtor within 30 days of the expiry of the period for denying claims (Section 124(4)).

faq.q: The debtor holds goods of ours subject to retention of title. Will we get them back?
faq.a: The Slovak Act offers two routes. The first is exclusion of the item from the inventory of assets: a person claiming that an item does not belong in the inventory may assert this with the trustee no later than the distribution of the proceeds from the realisation of that item (Section 78(3) of Act No. 7/2005 Coll.); the trustee calls on that person to state the reasons and submit evidence within 30 days of delivery of the call, and if the trustee does not accept them, the court, on the trustee’s application, orders that person to file, within a period of not less than 30 days, an action against the trustee to exclude the item from the estate (vylučovacia žaloba) — if the action is not filed in time, the inclusion of the item in the inventory is presumed to be undisputed (Section 78(2) and (4)). The seller cannot, however, claim the return of the item if the trustee performs the obligations under the contract without undue delay after being called on by the seller to do so (Section 45a(2)); if the item is no longer with the bankrupt, the claims can be asserted only by lodging them (Section 45a(4)). The second route is Section 29(9): the seller may assert its rights by lodging a claim in the same way as it would assert a security right — it thereby entrusts the trustee with entering the item in the inventory and realising it, and has a position similar to that of a secured creditor. If the item has been realised, the person with a right that excludes its entry in the inventory is entitled to the proceeds (Section 78(8)). Whether the retention of title validly arose depends on the applicable law, which need not be Slovak law; where the contract is governed by Slovak law, the retention of title must be agreed in writing (Section 445 of the Commercial Code). If at the time of the opening of proceedings the goods were situated in a Member State other than Slovakia, the opening of proceedings does not, under Article 10(1) of Regulation (EU) 2015/848, affect the seller’s rights based on the retention of title.

faq.q: The debtor paid us shortly before the bankruptcy. Can we lose that money?
faq.a: It can happen, but not automatically. The trustee — and, if the trustee does not act on a creditor’s suggestion within a reasonable time, also a creditor with a lodged claim — may contest legal acts of the debtor that curtail the satisfaction of lodged claims (Section 57(1) and (4) of Act No. 7/2005 Coll.). With payments, what mainly comes into consideration is a preferential legal act under Section 59(1): an act by which the debtor performed a monetary claim that would otherwise have fallen due only upon the declaration of bankruptcy, secured its obligation later than it arose, or otherwise unjustifiably favoured its creditor over other creditors. It can be contested if it caused the debtor’s insolvency (úpadok) or was made while the debtor was insolvent, and only if it was made during the one year before the commencement of bankruptcy proceedings; for acts in favour of persons related to the debtor the period is three years (Section 59(3) and (4)). The right to contest is extinguished unless it is asserted against the obliged person or in court within one year of the declaration of bankruptcy (Section 57(2)). The creditor also has a defence under Article 16 of Regulation (EU) 2015/848: the rules of the State of the opening of proceedings on the avoidance (contestability) of legal acts do not apply where the person who benefited from the act proves that the act is subject to the law of another Member State and that the law of that Member State does not allow any means of challenging the act in the relevant case. We arrange the assessment of the foreign law in cooperation with the client’s lawyer in the client’s own country.

faq.q: How much of the claim will we receive?
faq.a: No estimate can be given in advance — it depends on the debtor’s assets, on the amount of the other claims and on the ranking of yours. The Act determines only the order of priority. From the proceeds, claims against the estate are paid first, in particular the costs of realisation and distribution, the trustee’s remuneration and expenses, and obligations that arose after the declaration of bankruptcy in administering the assets and operating the business (Section 87 of Act No. 7/2005 Coll.). A secured creditor is satisfied from the proceeds of the assets securing its claim (the separate estate) and, as to the unsatisfied remainder, as an unsecured creditor (Section 94). Unsecured claims are satisfied from the general estate and, if the proceeds are insufficient, proportionately to their respective amounts (Section 95(1)). Only after them come subordinated claims, among which the Act also ranks contractual penalties and claims of persons related to the bankrupt (Section 95(2) and (3)). The distribution cannot award a creditor more than it asserted in the lodgement (Section 96(1)). In restructuring the extent and timing of satisfaction are determined by the plan; the court rejects it if any unsecured claim — other than those that would be subordinated in bankruptcy — is to be satisfied as to less than 50 % or over a period longer than five years without the written consent of the creditor concerned (Section 154(1)(g) and (h)).

faq.q: It is not bankruptcy but restructuring that is under way. How is that different for us?
faq.a: A debtor in restructuring continues in business, and creditors are satisfied under a plan on which they themselves vote and which the court confirms. For a foreign supplier four differences follow. The period is shorter — 30 days from the authorisation of the restructuring — and there is no late lodging: a claim lodged after the period is disregarded (Section 121 of Act No. 7/2005 Coll.), and after confirmation of the plan a claim that was not lodged cannot be recovered from the debtor (Section 120(1), Section 155(2)). A claim may be denied only by the trustee, and the action for its determination is filed against the debtor within 30 days of the expiry of the period for denying claims (Section 124(2) and (4)). From the commencement of restructuring proceedings onwards it is not possible, on account of old debts, to terminate the contract by notice or withdraw from it, to set off, or to commence enforcement (Section 114(1)); a party that is to perform first may refuse performance until the counter-performance is provided or secured (Section 114(3)). Conversely, claims that arise only during the restructuring proceedings are priority claims: they are not lodged and the plan does not affect them without the creditor’s consent; what counts is the moment the right to performance arose, not the due date (Section 120(2)). If the court rejects the plan by a final decision, it declares bankruptcy over the debtor’s assets (Section 154(3)); the Act does not provide that a lodgement made in the restructuring is treated as a lodgement in the bankruptcy, so we monitor the bankruptcy deadline separately.

xen.metaTitle: Enforcement in Slovakia for foreign creditors
xen.metaDescription: Enforcing an EU judgment, a European order for payment or an arbitral award in Slovakia. Defending a company against enforcement. Law firm in Zvolen.
xen.heroTitle: Enforcing a foreign judgment in Slovakia — and defending a foreign company against Slovak enforcement
xen.heroLead: You hold a judgment, a European order for payment or an arbitral award, and your debtor has assets in Slovakia. Where the enforcement title comes from a Member State of the European Union, there is no need to sue again in Slovakia or to apply for a declaration of enforceability — an application for enforcement is filed directly. And if the enforcement is directed against your company, you have 15 days from service of the notice of commencement of enforcement to file an application to stop the enforcement with suspensive effect.
heroPara: We act for foreign companies in Slovak enforcement proceedings on both sides: as the creditor (oprávnený) enforcing in Slovakia a claim awarded by a foreign title, and as the debtor (povinný) against whom enforcement is being conducted in Slovakia or against whom a payment order (platobný rozkaz) has been issued. We advise exclusively on Slovak law; documents issued by the court of the State in which the title originated are obtained by the client in its own State, as a rule with its local lawyer, with whom we work together.
We work in English and Slovak and can run the whole matter remotely.
xen.heroCta: Send us your title for assessment
xen.whoTitle: Two sides of the same proceedings
xen.whoLead: This page is intended for foreign companies that are not familiar with Slovak law: creditors who already hold an enforcement title and need to have it enforced in Slovakia, and companies that have received a document from Slovakia with a short time limit.

who.title: A creditor holding a judgment or a European order for payment
who.desc: You hold an enforceable judgment of a court of an EU Member State, a European order for payment or a European Enforcement Order, and the debtor has its registered office, a bank account, real estate or customers in Slovakia. Enforceability is not separately declared in Slovakia; an application for enforcement is filed directly.

who.title: A creditor holding an arbitral award
who.desc: An arbitral award made outside Slovakia — in an EU Member State or outside the EU. It is recognised directly in the enforcement proceedings, without a separate decision on recognition; what matters is whether the documents are complete and whether the debtor proves one of the statutory grounds for refusal.

who.title: A company that has received a notice of commencement of enforcement or a Slovak payment order
who.desc: The time limits are short — as a rule 15 days from service — and in enforcement proceedings a missed time limit is not excused. We need to know the date of service and to see everything that was served on you.

who.title: A company whose Slovak subsidiary is in a dispute
who.desc: A Slovak limited liability company (s.r.o.) is a separate legal entity with its own official electronic mailbox (elektronická schránka), into which the Slovak courts serve documents. A document may be deemed served even if no one has opened it. We check the status of the proceedings and enforcements pending against the subsidiary and the time limits running in them.

xen.keyTitle: What title you hold — and what follows from it in Slovakia
xen.keyLead: In Slovakia, the compulsory enforcement of decisions is governed by Act No. 233/1995 Coll. (the Enforcement Code — Exekučný poriadok). Enforcement is carried out not by the court but by an enforcement officer (súdny exekútor) — under Section 2(1) of the Act, a person designated and empowered by the State to carry out the compulsory enforcement of enforcement titles — whom the court authorises to carry out the enforcement. A single court, the District Court Banská Bystrica, has exclusive subject-matter jurisdiction over enforcement proceedings for the whole territory of Slovakia (Section 49). Under Section 45(2)(b), a foreign enforcement title enforceable in the Slovak Republic is also an enforcement title. What has to be attached to the application, and how the debtor can defend itself, depends on where the title comes from.

key.title: Judgment of a court of an EU Member State — no declaration of enforceability
key.desc: Under Article 39 of Regulation (EU) No 1215/2012 (Brussels I bis), a judgment given in a Member State which is enforceable in that Member State is enforceable in the other Member States without any declaration of enforceability being required. Under Article 41(1), it is enforced in the Member State addressed under the same conditions as a judgment given in that State — in Slovakia, therefore, in enforcement proceedings. Under Article 2(a), a judgment is any judgment given by a court or tribunal of a Member State, whatever the judgment may be called. For the purposes of enforcement, the applicant provides under Article 42(1) a copy of the judgment which satisfies the conditions necessary to establish its authenticity, and the certificate issued pursuant to Article 53, certifying that the judgment is enforceable and containing an extract of the judgment as well as, where appropriate, relevant information on the recoverable costs of the proceedings and the calculation of interest. The certificate is issued by the court of origin, at the request of any interested party, using the form set out in Annex I to the Regulation (Article 53) — it is therefore requested in the State in which the judgment was given, not in Slovakia. The competent enforcement authority may, where necessary, require a translation or a transliteration of the contents of the certificate (Article 42(3)); it may require a translation of the judgment itself only if it is unable to proceed without such a translation (Article 42(4)). The translation is made into the official language of the Member State addressed, that is, into Slovak (Article 57(1)), and is done by a person qualified to do translations in one of the Member States (Article 57(3)). Under Article 46, enforcement of a judgment is refused only on the application of the person against whom enforcement is sought, where one of the grounds referred to in Article 45 is found to exist: manifest conflict with public policy; a judgment given in default of appearance where the defendant was not served with the document which instituted the proceedings in sufficient time and in such a way as to enable the defendant to arrange for a defence (unless the defendant failed to commence proceedings to challenge the judgment when it was possible to do so); irreconcilability with another judgment between the same parties; or conflict with certain rules of jurisdiction.
key.note: Under Article 66(1), the Regulation applies to legal proceedings instituted on or after 10 January 2015; under Article 66(2), Regulation (EC) No 44/2001 continues to apply to judgments given in proceedings instituted earlier. Under Article 43(1), the certificate is served on the person against whom enforcement is sought prior to the first enforcement measure, and is accompanied by the judgment if it has not already been served on that person; the Enforcement Code follows on from this in Section 61a(2), under which the foreign enforcement title is attached to the notice of commencement of enforcement if it has not already been served on the debtor. The applicant cannot be required to have a postal address in the Member State addressed (Article 41(3)).

key.title: European order for payment, European Enforcement Order and the European Small Claims Procedure
key.desc: Under Article 19 of Regulation (EC) No 1896/2006, a European order for payment which has become enforceable in the Member State of origin is recognised and enforced in the other Member States without the need for a declaration of enforceability and without any possibility of opposing its recognition. It is declared enforceable by the court of origin using standard form G if no statement of opposition has been lodged with that court within 30 days of service of the order on the defendant (Article 18(1) in conjunction with Article 16(2)). For enforcement in another Member State, the claimant provides under Article 21(2) a copy of the European order for payment, as declared enforceable by the court of origin, which satisfies the conditions necessary to establish its authenticity, and, where necessary, a translation of it into the official language of the Member State of enforcement, certified by a person qualified to do so in one of the Member States. The order is enforced under the same conditions as an enforceable decision issued in the Member State of enforcement (Article 21(1)). Enforcement may be refused, on application by the defendant, only on the grounds set out in Article 22: because the order is irreconcilable with an earlier decision or order involving the same cause of action between the same parties, where the irreconcilability could not have been raised as an objection in the proceedings in the Member State of origin, or because the defendant has already paid the amount awarded in the order — to the extent that the defendant has done so. Under no circumstances may the European order for payment be reviewed as to its substance in the Member State of enforcement (Article 22(3)).
key.note: A judgment on an uncontested claim which has been certified as a European Enforcement Order in the Member State of origin is likewise enforced without a declaration of enforceability and without any possibility of opposing its recognition (Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 805/2004; the creditor provides a copy of the judgment and a copy of the certificate under Article 20(2)), as is a judgment given in the European Small Claims Procedure (Article 20(1) of Regulation (EC) No 861/2007). With these, too, the judgment may not be reviewed as to its substance in the Member State of enforcement (Article 21(2) of Regulation No 805/2004, Article 22(2) of Regulation No 861/2007).

key.title: Slovak enforcement proceedings: one court, an electronic application, an enforcement officer selected at random
key.desc: The application for enforcement is filed with the District Court Banská Bystrica by electronic means, into the court's official electronic mailbox, using the electronic form designated for that purpose; the application must be authorised (autorizovaný) — as a rule with a qualified electronic signature or a qualified electronic seal (Section 23(1) of Act No. 305/2013 Coll. on e-Government) — otherwise it is disregarded (Section 48(7) of the Enforcement Code). The enforcement title and public documents are attached as an authorised original electronic document or as an electronic document created by certified conversion (zaručená konverzia) of the original paper document (Section 48(6)). Certified conversion is the transformation of a paper document into electronic form with the aim of preserving its legal effects; a lawyer (advokát) is also entitled to carry it out (Section 35(2) and (3)(b) of Act No. 305/2013 Coll.). Attached to the application are a counterpart (rovnopis) of the enforcement title together with confirmation of its enforceability (Section 48(4)(a)), with which a foreign enforcement title is furnished by the authority of the State in which it was issued (Section 46(1)(c)), and, in the case of a foreign enforcement title, also the documents specified in special legislation; where the title has been certified under EU regulations and no decision on enforceability is required for its enforcement, the certificate is attached (Section 48(5)) — for a judgment from an EU Member State it is precisely the certificate under Article 53 that certifies its enforceability (Article 42(1)(b) of the Brussels I bis Regulation). A foreign legal entity evidences its identification data by an attached extract from the register or other record in which it is entered (Section 48(3)(b)). In the case of a foreign enforcement title for whose enforcement EU regulations require a certificate, the court proceeds in the same way as with a Slovak title: unless there are grounds for dismissing the application, it issues the authorisation to carry out enforcement (poverenie) within 15 days of receiving the application (Section 53(1) and (2)(c)). The court assigns cases to enforcement officers at random, using technical and software means, in such a way as to exclude any possibility of influencing the assignment of cases (Section 55(1)), namely to an enforcement officer appointed for the territorial district of the regional court in which the debtor, where it is a legal entity, has its registered office (Section 55(2)(b)) — the creditor does not choose the enforcement officer. The enforcement commences when the authorisation is delivered to the enforcement officer (Section 57(1)). A monetary claim may be enforced by deductions from wages and other income, by attachment of a claim — including a claim arising from a bank account and other monetary claims of the debtor — and by sale of movable property, securities, real estate or a business (Section 63(1), Section 93(1)); enforcement may also be levied against the debtor's share in a company (Section 113b(1)).
key.note: The debtor's assets are identified by the enforcement officer. Third parties are obliged to cooperate with the enforcement officer at the officer's request if the officer has produced to them the authorisation to carry out enforcement (Section 42(1)): banks notify the officer of the debtor's account numbers, their balances and changes in them (Section 42(6)), and data are also provided by the authority keeping the register of real estate, the authority keeping the register of motor vehicles and the central securities depository (Section 42(4)). In identifying assets, the enforcement officer takes the creditor's instructions into account (Section 59(1)); the officer submits the first report on the findings to the creditor no later than three months after the commencement of enforcement, and further reports at 180-day intervals (Section 59(3)). After service of the notice of commencement of enforcement, assets subject to enforcement may not be disposed of without the enforcement officer's prior written consent, with the exception of ordinary legal transactions (Section 61d(1)).

key.title: Foreign arbitral award — recognition directly in the enforcement proceedings
key.desc: Under Section 46(1) of Act No. 244/2002 Coll. on arbitration, a foreign arbitral award is an arbitral decision on the merits made in the territory of a State other than the Slovak Republic — irrespective of whether that State is an EU Member State; under its Article 1(2)(d), the Brussels I bis Regulation does not apply to arbitration. Recognition of a foreign arbitral award is not pronounced by a separate decision: the award is recognised by the court having jurisdiction over enforcement taking it into account as if it were a domestic arbitral award (Section 49(1)), and it is enforced as a domestic arbitral award (Section 49(2)). Under Section 47(1), the party is required to attach to the application the original of the foreign arbitral award or a certified copy of it, and the original of the arbitration agreement or a certified copy of it; if they are not drawn up in the Slovak language, the party arranges for an official translation of them (Section 47(2)). Because this is not a title for which a certificate under EU regulations suffices, the court, under Section 54(1) of the Enforcement Code, serves the foreign enforcement title personally (do vlastných rúk) on the person named as the debtor before issuing the authorisation and informs that person of the possibility of raising grounds for non-recognition. If that person does not state them within 15 days of service of that information, the court examines the conditions for recognition and enforcement which it examines even of its own motion, and if it finds no obstacles and there are no grounds for dismissing the application, it issues the authorisation to carry out enforcement (Section 54(2)).
key.note: The grounds for refusing recognition and enforcement are set out in Section 50 of the Act. On the application of the party against whom the award is invoked, the court may refuse recognition and enforcement only if that party proves that it lacked the capacity to conclude the arbitration agreement or that the agreement was not concluded in accordance with the applicable law; that it was not given proper notice of the appointment of the arbitrator or of the arbitral proceedings, or was not given the opportunity to take part in them; that the award decided a dispute for which the arbitration agreement had not been concluded or which does not fall within the scope of the arbitration clause; that the arbitral tribunal was not constituted, or the proceedings were not conducted, in the agreed manner; or that the award has not become final and binding, or has been set aside, or its enforcement has been suspended by a court of the State of origin (Section 50(1)). The court refuses recognition and enforcement even without an application if, under Slovak law, the subject matter of the dispute cannot be resolved in arbitration, or if recognition and enforcement would be contrary to public policy (Section 50(2)). Under Section 53, the Act applies unless an international treaty by which the Slovak Republic is bound provides otherwise; as an example of such a treaty the Act cites the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (Decree of the Minister of Foreign Affairs No. 74/1959 Coll.), known as the New York Convention.

key.title: Judgment from a non-EU State — the Act on private international and procedural law
key.desc: Judgments from States to which the EU regulations do not apply are governed by Act No. 97/1963 Coll. on private international and procedural law — under its Section 2, however, only where an international treaty by which the Slovak Republic is bound does not provide otherwise. Under Section 63, foreign decisions have effect in the Slovak Republic if they have been recognised by the Slovak authorities. A decision in a property matter does not require recognition by a separate ruling: under Section 67(3), it is recognised by the Slovak court issuing the authorisation to carry out enforcement. The court decides on recognition by a separate ruling only on application (Section 67(4)); jurisdiction lies with the court that has jurisdiction to issue the authorisation to carry out enforcement (Section 68a(c)). Under Section 64, a foreign decision cannot be recognised or enforced if recognition is precluded by the exclusive jurisdiction of the Slovak authorities, or if the authority of the foreign State would not have had jurisdiction to decide had its jurisdiction been assessed under the provisions of Slovak law; if the decision is not final or enforceable in the State in which it was issued; if it is not a decision on the merits; if the party against whom the decision is to be recognised was deprived, by the procedure of the foreign authority, of the opportunity to act before that authority, in particular where the summons or the application initiating the proceedings was not duly served on that party; if a Slovak court has already given a final decision in the matter, or there is an earlier foreign decision in the same matter which has been recognised or meets the conditions for recognition; or if recognition would be contrary to Slovak public policy. Review of the foreign decision on the merits is not permitted (Section 68f(2)). In enforcement proceedings the court proceeds under Section 54 of the Enforcement Code: it serves the foreign enforcement title on the debtor, who has 15 days to state grounds precluding recognition or enforcement, or to file an application for separate recognition.
key.note: For the United Kingdom, the date on which the proceedings were instituted is decisive: under Article 67(2)(a) of the Agreement on the withdrawal of the United Kingdom from the European Union, the Brussels I bis Regulation applies to the recognition and enforcement of judgments given in legal proceedings instituted before the end of the transition period, which under Article 126 of the Agreement ended on 31 December 2020. In addition, by Council Decision (EU) 2022/1206 the European Union approved its accession to the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Judgments in Civil or Commercial Matters, concluded on 2 July 2019 under the auspices of the Hague Conference on Private International Law; according to the declaration which the Union makes on accession, its Member States, with the exception of Denmark, will be bound by the Convention by virtue of that accession. Whether, and from when, the Convention applies in relation to the particular State of origin of a judgment is something we verify separately in each matter. A person applying for recognition by a separate ruling attaches, under Section 68c(2) of Act No. 97/1963 Coll., the original or an officially certified copy of the foreign decision in full, a confirmation from the competent foreign authority that it is final or enforceable, documentary evidence that the obstacle under Section 64(d) does not exist, and officially certified translations into the Slovak language; under item 18d of the schedule of court fees, the court fee for such an application is 100 euros.

key.title: The debtor's defence: 15 days from service
key.desc: If your company is the debtor in a Slovak enforcement, the first document from the enforcement officer is the notice of commencement of enforcement. It must contain, among other things, the amount of the costs if the enforced obligation is performed within 15 days of service and the amount of the costs after that period has expired, information on the possibility of filing an application to stop the enforcement and on the time limit until the expiry of which that application has suspensive effect, and — in the case of a foreign decision for which no declaration of enforceability is required — also information on the possibility of objecting to its recognition or enforcement (Section 61a(1)(e) to (g) and (i) of the Enforcement Code). The debtor may file an application to stop the enforcement within 15 days of service of the notice; it must state reasons, it must set out all the facts that the debtor can rely on as at the date of filing, and such an application has suspensive effect (Section 61k(2)). It is filed with the enforcement officer (Section 61k(5)) and the court decides on it as a matter of priority (Section 61l(1)). The court stops the enforcement on the grounds set out in Section 61k(1): after the enforcement title came into existence, circumstances arose which caused the enforced claim to be extinguished; the enforcement title has been set aside; there is a ground under special legislation on which recognition or enforcement of the foreign enforcement title is inadmissible, unless it could have been raised earlier in the proceedings; or there are other facts which prevent the enforcement title from being enforced. In applications filed later, the debtor may rely only on facts that arose after the 15-day period expired, or on facts that, through no fault of its own, it could not have raised earlier (Section 61k(3)); later applications do not have suspensive effect (Section 61k(4)(a)). In enforcement proceedings, a missed time limit cannot be excused (Section 201(1)(a)).
key.note: Suspensive effect does not mean that the enforcement officer takes no action: under Section 61i(1) and (3), the officer retains the power to carry out acts aimed at identifying and securing assets. A bank account may therefore be blocked up to the amount of the claim and its accessories (Section 95(1)(a)); however, the enforcement officer issues the order (exekučný príkaz) upon service of which the bank pays the claim out to the officer only after the period for filing an application to stop the enforcement with suspensive effect has expired without such an application being filed, or after service of the court's decision dismissing such an application (Section 96(1) and (3)). If a debtor who has filed an application to stop the enforcement deposits security equal to the value of the enforced claim in the enforcement officer's special account, the enforcement is suspended and the officer does not carry out acts aimed at securing assets and, if they have already been carried out, cancels them (Section 61h(1)(f), Section 61i(2)). For a payment order issued by a Slovak court, the time limit for a statement of opposition is 15 days from service and the opposition must be reasoned on the merits, otherwise the court rejects it (Section 265(1) and Section 267(1) and (2) of the Civil Contentious Procedure Code; in payment order proceedings, Section 7(2), Section 11(1) and Section 12(1) of Act No. 307/2016 Coll.). In payment order proceedings (upomínacie konanie) — simplified electronic proceedings before the District Court Banská Bystrica — the application is not admissible if the payment order would have to be served on the defendant abroad (Section 3(6)(d)). For a European order for payment, the time limit for a statement of opposition is 30 days from service and the defendant does not have to specify the reasons in it (Article 16(2) and (3) of Regulation (EC) No 1896/2006).

steps.title: Assessment of the title
steps.desc: We establish which regime your title falls under — an EU regulation, the Act on arbitration or the Act on private international and procedural law — as well as whether it is enforceable in the State of origin and which documents are still missing. For titles that became enforceable more than three years ago, we keep watch on Section 53(3)(g) and (4) of the Enforcement Code: the court dismisses the application in so far as it concerns recurring accessories (as a rule default interest) to which entitlement arose after the title became enforceable, if the application is filed more than three years after the title became enforceable without the debtor having been called on to satisfy the claim in the last three months before the application was filed, or without an agreement on satisfaction of the claim in instalments having been concluded with the debtor within three years of the title becoming enforceable. We therefore send the demand to satisfy the claim before the application is filed.

steps.title: Checking the debtor
steps.desc: Before filing the application we check what can be ascertained from public sources: the commercial register, which is a public list (Section 3(1) of Act No. 29/2026 Coll.), the financial statements filed in the public part of the register of financial statements (Section 23c(1) of Act No. 431/2002 Coll.), the land registry (kataster), which everyone has the right to inspect (Section 68(1) of Act No. 162/1995 Coll.), the register of authorisations to carry out enforcement, in which the Ministry of Justice publishes data from the authorisations issued for the duration of the enforcement (Section 56(3) of the Enforcement Code), and whether bankruptcy or restructuring proceedings are pending against the debtor. Data on bank accounts are disclosed by banks only to an enforcement officer who produces the authorisation (Section 42(1) and (6) of the Enforcement Code).

steps.title: Documents, translations and conversion
steps.desc: We tell you in writing exactly what to request from the court of origin — the certificate under Article 53 of the Brussels I bis Regulation, the European order for payment declared enforceable on form G, or the European Enforcement Order certificate. The issue of these documents is governed by the law of the State of origin; it is handled by your local lawyer or directly by your company. In Slovakia we arrange the official translation into Slovak where one is needed, and the certified conversion of paper documents into electronic form.

steps.title: Application for enforcement
steps.desc: We file the application electronically with the District Court Banská Bystrica. The court fee for the application is 25 euros (item 13(a) of the schedule of court fees); the court does not call on the applicant to pay it, and if the fee is not paid in full within 15 days of filing, the application is disregarded (Section 11d(2) and (3) of Act No. 71/1992 Coll.). The court issues the authorisation to carry out enforcement and assigns the case to an enforcement officer at random. The enforcement officer notifies the creditor and the debtor of the commencement of enforcement and calls on the debtor to satisfy the enforced claim (Section 61(1) of the Enforcement Code).

steps.title: The course of the enforcement — and the defence, if you are on the other side
steps.desc: We communicate with the enforcement officer, pass on to the officer what you know about the debtor's assets and follow the officer's reports. If the debtor applies to stop the enforcement, the enforcement officer calls on the creditor to comment within a period of not less than ten days (Section 61k(5) of the Enforcement Code); we prepare the comments. If you are the debtor in the proceedings, the procedure is the mirror image: immediately after service of the notice of commencement of enforcement or of the payment order we establish the date of service, assess the enforcement title, the manner in which it was served and the enforced claim, and within the time limit file an application to stop the enforcement or a statement of opposition.

For an arbitral award, also the arbitration agreement or the contract containing the arbitration clause.

We quote the fee before any work starts; if you decide not to go ahead, the matter ends there.

price.label: Representation in proceedings
price.desc: Under Section 7(1) of Decree of the Ministry of Justice of the Slovak Republic No. 655/2004 Coll., a contingency fee may be agreed in the form of a percentage share in the value of the matter; under Section 7(2) its maximum amount may not exceed 20 % of that value. Under Section 8(1) of the Decree it becomes payable only where the client has been fully successful in the matter; where the client is partly successful the lawyer is entitled under Section 8(2) to the tariff fee determined according to the degree of success, and where the client has not been successful even in part the lawyer may under Section 8(3) claim only reimbursement of out-of-pocket expenses.

xen.priceNote: Out-of-pocket expenses arise alongside the lawyer's fee — in particular the court fee, official translations and certified conversion of documents. The court fee for an application for enforcement is 25 euros under item 13(a) of the schedule to Act No. 71/1992 Coll. The enforcement officer's costs consist of the officer's fee and reimbursement of expenses (Section 196 of the Enforcement Code); where a monetary performance is being enforced, the fee is determined as a percentage of the amount recovered and may not exceed the amount of the enforced claim (Section 197(1)). The enforcement officer's costs are paid by the debtor (Section 199c(4)). However, if the enforcement is stopped on a ground for which the enforcement officer issues a notice stopping the enforcement (upovedomenie o zastavení exekúcie) — for example, because no assets that could be reached by enforcement were identified — the creditor pays the enforcement officer reimbursement of expenses (Section 199c(1) in conjunction with Section 198(2)). The enforcement officer may require an advance on necessary expenses from the creditor only in the case of enforcement by sale of movable property, real estate or a business, and in the case of non-monetary performance (Section 58(1)). The outcome of enforcement depends on the circumstances of the individual case, in particular on the debtor's assets.
